title: Temporal splits and look-ahead prevention
objectives: Construct an expanding-history synthetic temporal fold with feature-availability checks, strict pre-test label maturity and explicit exclusions/window boundaries.
Keep preprocessing/model selection inside training folds and distinguish row gaps, time/label overlap, revisions and final held-out evaluation.
Apply temporal splits and look-ahead prevention invariants safely and identify scope boundaries.
motivation: A chronological row order is necessary for many forecasting tasks, but not sufficient to prevent leakage. A decision row can contain a revised future feature or a label measured over future events.

blocks.md: A chronological row order is necessary for many forecasting tasks, but not sufficient to prevent leakage. A decision row can contain a revised future feature or a label measured over future events. Define feature availability, decision time, label observation end and label availability separately. This own splitter assumes integer-clock same-asset synthetic samples with one scalar feature, not exchange calendars or a full financial purged cross-validator.

Test decisions lie in [start,end). Training decisions must be earlier than start, with BOTH label_end<start and label_available<start. Strict inequality is deliberate: labels arriving exactly at the test start are not assumed processed before that decision. Each feature must already be available by its own decision time, or the whole dataset fails validation. A test label can arrive after the test period for later scoring; it is never fed into training. No fitting occurs inside the splitter.

blocks.title: A past row can still carry future information
items: Test decisions are [6,8). Row a (decision 1, label_end 2, label_available 2) can train. Row b (decision 2, end 4, available 6) cannot: the label arrives exactly at start 6 and this strict contract requires earlier availability.
Row c (decision 4, end 7, available 8) also cannot train even though its decision precedes 6. Row d (decision 6) belongs to test; row e (decision 8) is outside the half-open test window.

Only a trains, so training center=10. Test d feature 100 transforms to 90. If you improperly fit a center on train+test, you get 55, letting test features affect the learned transform. A fixed no-fit unit conversion is different from learning a statistic.

blocks.caption: Expected train ('a',), test ('d',); excluded b/c training-label-not-known-before-test, e after-test-window; training mean 10, test centered Fraction(90,1); leaky combined mean 55; invalid sample information clocks. Full source, max 128 rows, strict exact ints/no bool, unique sample IDs, deterministic decision/id ordering. No equal-spacing assumption used by this own time-boundary selector. Code shows the bad combined mean only as a labeled counterexample, not a recommended preprocessing pipeline.

blocks.md: scikit-learn TimeSeriesSplit trains on preceding folds and exposes gap as a NUMBER OF SAMPLES excluded before test. Its comparable-duration interpretation requires equally spaced observations. A row gap is not automatically hours/days on irregular data, nor does it inspect label maturity, feature revisions or economic event overlap. A sufficient gap for one fixed horizon can be insufficient for variable horizons. Our explicit label-end/available checks address one chosen expanding-history boundary, not every dependency/shared-event leakage mode.

Within EACH fold, fit imputation/scaling/PCA/feature selection and the model using eligible training data only, then transform/test without refitting on test. The same preprocessing TYPE does not mean fitting the same combined data. A pipeline helps enforce this when fitted on the right split, but cannot repair future-bearing raw features, wrong labels or an invalid universe. For training features, use the feature snapshot at each historical decision, not today's final correction.

Use earlier temporal validation folds to choose hyperparameters/features/cost assumptions, and keep a final later holdout untouched until the choice is frozen. Repeatedly inspect the final score and revise the strategy, and it becomes part of model selection even without calling fit on it. If retuning is planned over time, simulate the actual retraining schedule and available labels. Do not claim a one-time split proves a stable future regime or fixes multiple-testing bias.

The splitter removes training labels ending/available at or after test start. It does not assert independence of remaining observations. Overlapping features, shared issuers/events, serial dependence, cross-sectional panel timing and market regimes require task-specific evaluation and uncertainty. A post-test embargo is not implemented here because this expanding training set never trains on future rows relative to that test. Other resampling designs need their own interval rules; do not call a row gap a universal embargo.

Independent transfer: move b label availability from 6 to 5 and confirm it becomes eligible;move a feature availability later than its decision and require a dataset error. Permute samples and verify identical fold content; test start/end boundaries, empty training and overlapping labels. Fit a mean or scaler only on each fold's eligible training rows, record fitted parameters, and prove changing held-out feature values cannot change those parameters. Keep final-holdout reuse and outcomes uncertainty explicit.

Sources: [TimeSeriesSplit row-gap/equal-spacing semantics](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.model_selection.TimeSeriesSplit.html), [scikit-learn leakage and train-only preprocessing](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html), [ALFRED point-in-time revisions](https://alfred.stlouisfed.org/help/downloaddata). This own strict label-aware splitter is not the scikit-learn algorithm and has no scikit-learn dependency.

guidedExercise.prompt: Why can an ordered dataset and a fixed row gap still give an optimistic historical evaluation?
hints: Distinguishes row gap and elapsed time.
guidedExercise.solution: Features may contain future revisions/unavailable values, labels may overlap or arrive after training cutoff, irregular spacing changes time represented by the row gap, and global preprocessing/test-guided selection can leak. Need point-in-time raw features, explicit label/availability interval checks, train-only fitted transforms and honest held-out/model-selection protocol. Remaining dependence/regime uncertainty persists.

independentExercise.prompt: Write a small test case that deliberately breaks the contract boundary in "Temporal splits and look-ahead prevention" and verify how your implementation rejects or handles it.
hints: Test zero, negative, empty, duplicate, and boundary values.
Confirm both time/memory complexity and numerical precision remain within spec.

commonMistakes: Boundary policy must match the simulated decision/ingestion order. (The own boundary is deliberately strict.)
Split first and fit learned preprocessing within each fold. (Apply those fitted parameters to the test.)
Only a; b is available exactly at 6 and c crosses/arrives later.
realWorldApplication: Used directly across production quantitative research, execution systems, and validation pipelines.
quantFinanceApplication: Applies rigorous engineering contracts to quantitative modeling and live trading infrastructure.
summary: Historical decision order does not establish information availability.
Exclude immature/crossing training labels under declared interval semantics, fit transforms only on each training fold, and preserve later holdout independence.
Row gaps are not universal time/label isolation and no split certifies future performance.

quiz.prompt: Under this strict start 6 contract, a past label becomes available exactly 6. Can it train?
options: Yes, because its decision was earlier
Only after observing the test score
Always, if its future value is favorable
quiz.explanation: Boundary policy must match the simulated decision/ingestion order. (The own boundary is deliberately strict.)

quiz.prompt: Where should a learned scaler be fit for a temporal fold?
options: All rows to make scaling stable
quiz.explanation: Split first and fit learned preprocessing within each fold. (Apply those fitted parameters to the test.)

quiz.prompt: How many training rows remain in the worked [6,8) fold?
quiz.explanation: Only a; b is available exactly at 6 and c crosses/arrives later.

quiz.prompt: What is scikit-learn TimeSeriesSplit gap measured in?
options: Samples excluded from the training tail
Elapsed time between observations, inferred automatically from date values
quiz.explanation: Row counts require spacing/horizon interpretation. (It is not inherently elapsed calendar time.)

quiz.prompt: You repeatedly revise a strategy after seeing final holdout scores. What changed?
options: Only fitted model parameters can transmit test information; strategy revisions cannot
Nothing if fit() was not called
quiz.explanation: Information flow includes human/automated selection choices. (Reserve genuinely unseen later evidence or report reuse.)
